Looking at this position, let me analyze Black's tactical opportunities.

**Position Analysis:**
- Black Knight on e4 is actively placed
- Black Queen on d3 is menacing
- White King on g1 has limited escape squares (g2 has a pawn, f2 has a bishop)
- White just moved Rc1, but this doesn't address the real threat

**The Winning Move:**

**Ng3+** — This forces checkmate in two moves!

After 1...Ng3+ White has no legal king moves:
- Kf1 is blocked by the bishop on f2
- So Kh1 is forced

Then 2...Qf1# is checkmate! The queen delivers mate on f1—the king can't escape to g1 (queen controls it) or h2 (knight controls it).

**Coaching Note:**
Always look for forcing moves—especially checks! This knight check looked devastating because it severely restricted White's king options. Once you found that Kh1 was forced, your queen had a clear mating square. When tactical pieces (knights, queens) are actively placed near the enemy king, calculate forcing continuations carefully.
